{{Quote|Only twenty Jedi have ever left the Order.''"<br />"''The Lost Twenty. And Count Dooku was the most recent and the most painful. No one likes to talk about it. His leaving was a great loss to the Order.|[[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Jocasta Nu/Legends|Jocasta Nu]]|<ref name="Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)">[[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'' novelization]]</ref>}}
The '''Lost Twenty''', originally known as '''The Lost''', were the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]] who had voluntarily resigned from the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] over ideological differences.

==History==
{{Quote|You're one of the Lost Twenty. Like Dooku.''"<br />"''I am the twenty-first, Master Shryne. Surely you've heard of Anakin Skywalker. The Chosen One.|[[Roan Shryne]] and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]|<ref name="Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]''</ref>}}
[[File:DarthRuin-EGF.jpg|thumb|left|Darth Ruin, formerly known as Phanius, an early member of the Lost Twenty.]]

One of the earliest members of the Lost Twenty<ref name="JVS" /> was the [[Umbaran/Legends|Umbaran]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] Phanius, who eventually became [[Darth Ruin/Legends|Darth Ruin]], the founder of the [[New Sith]].<ref name="END">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/88/indexp2.html|text=''Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties''|int=Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties}}</ref> Over time more would leave; twelve by [[990 BBY]],<ref name="RoT">''[[Darth Bane: Rule of Two]]''</ref> and ending with the twentieth member, Master [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]], leaving the Order in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]<ref name="JVS" /> because of a growing disenchantment with the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="ROTS novel">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref> Dooku fell under the tutelage of the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] and became his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]],<ref name="AOTC">{{Film|II}}</ref> [[Darth/Legends|Darth]]<ref name="ROTS novel" /> Tyranus.<ref name="AOTC" /> Following the dissolution of the Order in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the fallen [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] Darth Vader, formerly [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], considered himself the twenty-first member of this group.<ref name="Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader" />

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Jedi Knight [[Bardan Jusik]], disenchanted with the Republic and the Jedi's treatment of their [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] soldiers and believing it to not be the Jedi way, also left the Order before Skywalker, though he was not counted as a member of the Lost Twenty because he was not yet a Master.<ref name="Republic Commando: True Colors">''[[Republic Commando: True Colors]]''</ref><!-- Darth Desolous did not resign his commission as a Master, he was expelled from the Order. Therefore, he is not a member of the Twenty.-->

Along with the most venerable Masters,<ref name="DB">{{DB|location|jediarchives|Jedi Archives}}</ref> the Lost were remembered in the form of [[Bronzium/Legends|bronzium]] busts in the [[Jedi Archives/Legends|Jedi Archives]], a reminder of the Jedi's greatest failures—though the Jedi did not fault the individuals for leaving, regarding the statues as a reminder that the Jedi were not perfect<ref name="RoT" /> and that sometimes they might fail to provide what a Jedi might seek out of life.<ref name="ROTS novel" /> Each bust's pedestal listed the great deeds of the Master it commemorated, but not the reason they left the Order.<ref name="RoT" />

Sidious later jotted down notes about the Twenty in the ''[[Book of Sith]]'' under [[Sorzus Syn]]'s diary section on the [[First Great Schism]], where he mentioned that the Lost Twenty were examples of Jedi who left the Order yet did not become combatants, while expressing his disgust at their philosophies being retained.<ref name="Book of Sith">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref>

Despite never achieving the rank of Jedi Master, Darth Vader considered himself to be the twenty-first member of the Lost and declared himself as such to a dying Jedi Master [[Roan Shryne]] after their duel on [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]].<ref name="Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:LeftSideBusts.jpg|thumb|right|Statues of possible members of the Lost Twenty.]]
According to [[Pablo Helman]] on the [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']] DVD commentary, during the scene where [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] speaks to [[Jocasta Nu/Legends|Jocasta Nu]], the room includes busts of himself, [[George Lucas]], [[Rob Coleman]], and [[John Knoll]]. It is not known whether any of these four were meant to represent any of the Lost Twenty.

In the [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)|novelization]] of ''Attack of the Clones'', Obi-Wan says that the Lost Twenty were the only Jedi to ever leave the Jedi Order, but ''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'' established that the Lost Twenty were exclusively Jedi Masters.
